samples.summary: Thumbnail-panel delete now double-moves the cursor: the heal fires first (backwards) and its own survivor choice (forwards) second
samples.evidence: thumbnail-panel.ts:320-323 does `store.batch(() => store.removeSlides([...targetIds]))` and only afterwards `editor.setCurrentSlide(nextCurrent)`. The batch notifies store listeners synchronously, and packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 responds with `editor.markDirty(); editor.render();` — which now runs `resolveCurrentSlide` and heals the cursor to `currentIndex - 1` (the slide BEFORE the deleted one), firing `currentSlideListeners` (presence broadcast at slides-view.tsx:1073-1094, thumbnail highlight, notes panel, toolbar refresh) and clearing selection. Line 321-322 then moves the cursor a second time to the panel's intended survivor (the first surviving slide AFTER the anchor, lines 315-318). Net effect for the user: a visible one-frame jump to the wrong slide, two `onCurrentSlideChange` notifications and two presence writes per delete. The delete path should either be made heal-aware or the heal should reuse the same survivor rule.

samples.summary: The heal fires listeners (and selection-change listeners) from inside render()/repaintOverlay(), so `broadcast` now issues a store write (`updatePresence` → `doc.update`) from within a render frame / store.onChange callback
samples.evidence: `resolveCurrentSlide` (editor.ts:1550-1554) calls `exitImageCrop(false)`, `exitEditMode('cancel')`, `setCellSelection(null)`, `selection.clear()` and `currentSlideListeners` while inside `render()`. `render()` is invoked from inside the store change callback at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 and from the RAF tick at :1115. The listeners registered at :1093-1095 all run `broadcast`, which calls `store.updatePresence` — and packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:2743-2752 documents that opening a nested `doc.update` while an update is open is illegal, guarding only the `activePresence` (batch) case, not the 'fired from inside a document-change subscription' case this change newly introduces. Previously current-slide listeners only ran from explicit user-driven `setCurrentSlide` / `setStore` calls, never from a render frame. Needs a runtime check against Yorkie (does the document-change subscriber run inside the update?) to confirm or refute.

samples.summary: Heal can clear the selection mid-gesture (repaintOverlay runs during pointer drags), while gestures keep a slideId/element captured at pointerdown and still commit on pointerup
samples.evidence: Gesture starters capture the slide and element up front — e.g. editor.ts:5701-5709 (`const startSlide = this.currentSlide(); … const slideId = startSlide.id;`) and editor.ts:4395 (`const slideId = this.currentSlide()?.id`) — and commit on pointerup. `repaintOverlay()` is called from pointermove handlers (e.g. editor.ts:4613) and now runs `resolveCurrentSlide`, which on a peer delete of the current slide calls `this.selection.clear()` and moves `currentId`. The in-flight gesture is not cancelled, so it commits to a slide that no longer exists with an already-cleared selection. Fix belongs on the new heal path (cancel active gestures alongside crop/text edit).

samples.summary: Heal direction (previous slide) contradicts the direction every other consumer uses when the current slide disappears (next surviving slide)
samples.evidence: The presenter lands on the slide AFTER the removed one — packages/slides/test/view/present/presenter.test.ts:1203-1205 removes `bId` and asserts `getCurrentSlideId() === cId`. thumbnail-panel.ts:313-318 likewise prefers 'the first surviving slide after the anchor'. The new editor heal at editor.ts:1534-1537 picks `currentIndex - 1`. Deleting the current slide from the canvas vs. the presenter vs. the thumbnail context menu now lands the user in different places.

verdict.reason: Verified the whole chain independently. thumbnail-panel.ts:302-326 computes the survivor before the mutation, then mutates at line 320 and only calls editor.setCurrentSlide(nextCurrent) at 321-323. memory.ts:1789-1803 and yorkie-slides-store.ts:598-629 both invoke notifyChange() synchronously at the close of the top-level batch, and notifyChange (memory.ts:1783-1787) runs listeners inline. slides-view.tsx:1051-1059 registers such a listener on the same store instance handed to mountThumbnailPanel (slides-view.tsx:1014-1019) and does editor.markDirty(); editor.render(). markDirty defeats the idle short-circuit at editor.ts:1413-1420, so render() reaches resolveCurrentSlide at editor.ts:1427, which for a missing id lands on currentIndex-1 (editor.ts:1534-1537), reassigns currentId (1544), clears cell + element selection (1552-1553) and fires currentSlideListeners (1554) -> presence broadcast via slides-view.tsx:1094/1073-1091. setCurrentSlide only early-returns when currentId already equals the target (editor.ts:1491-1492); at thumbnail-panel.ts:321 currentId is the deleted id, so the branch is entered, and the healed id differs from the panel's chosen survivor for any non-tail delete (e.g. [A,B,C], current B: heal -> A, then setCurrentSlide -> C). Result is two cursor moves, two onCurrentSlideChange notifications/presence writes and a transient frame on the wrong slide per delete. No guard exists (current-slide-heal.test.ts:167-225 covers only peer/undo removals). Real, in-lane (behaviour change to an exported symbol leaving another call site inconsistent), and blocking at major.

verdict.reason: The structural claim is accurate (the heal at editor.ts:1550-1554 fires currentSlideListeners from render()/repaintOverlay(), reached via slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 and :1115, and slides-view.tsx:1094 wires broadcast → store.updatePresence at :1079), but the claimed harm — an illegal nested doc.update — is not reachable. (a) The only re-entrant case, a listener firing while a batch's doc.update is open, is exactly what the existing guard covers: updatePresence folds into activePresence (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2748-2752), set by batch() at :616-624, with a regression test at packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:308-319. (b) The store.onChange path the finding says is unguarded never runs inside an open update: notifyChange() is only called from the remote-change subscriber (:364-369), from batch()'s finally AFTER doc.update has returned and batchDepth is 0 (:625-629), and from undo()/redo() after doc.history returns (:637-645); nested batches (:602-610) do not notify. So updatePresence there takes the ordinary standalone doc.update branch. (c) The repo already ships the exact pattern of a presence doc.update issued synchronously from inside a Yorkie document-change subscription: docs-view.tsx:365-381 calls store.publishResolvedLocalCursor from the remote-change handler, implemented as this.doc.update((_, p) => p.set(...)) at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1159-1170, fired from doc.subscribe's remote-change branch at yorkie-doc-store.ts:567-572. (d) The heal is idempotent (cursor moved first, editor.ts:1544-1546; settling asserted in packages/slides/test/view/editor/current-slide-heal.test.ts:215-225), so the RAF path cannot produce a per-frame presence write storm either.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed. repaintOverlay() resolves through the healing path (editor.ts:1065-1069 -> 1525-1556), and the heal branch moves currentId/currentIndex, cancels crop/text edit, clears cell selection and calls this.selection.clear() (editor.ts:1544-1553) with no check for an active pointer gesture (pointerInteractionActive is only consulted in hover logic, editor.ts:4644). Out-of-diff gesture handlers capture the slide at pointerdown and commit on pointerup with that captured id: startTableEdgeResize captures slideId at editor.ts:4395, repaints the overlay from its pointermove handler at editor.ts:4458, and commits store.updateTableColumnWidths/RowHeights(slideId, ...) at editor.ts:4476/4486; startConnectorEndpointDrag captures startSlide/slideId at editor.ts:5701-5709, reads this.selection.has() mid-drag at editor.ts:5766-5768, and commits updateConnectorEndpoint(slideId, ...) at editor.ts:6338. A commit against the vanished slide is not a silent no-op: requireSlideIndex throws "Slide not found" (store/memory.ts:1828-1832) via requireSlide in updateTableColumnWidths/updateTableRowHeights (memory.ts:1624, 1647). Nothing cancels the gesture on the heal: the only onCurrentSlideChange consumers are thumbnail-panel.ts:622 and notes-panel.ts:104, neither of which touches gesture state. So no already-guarded path exists, the code is present as described, and the issue is a changed-invariant/blast-radius concern rather than in-diff logic — blocking at major under this lens.
